title: feat(critique): make the critique lenses reach lite and delegate passes
body:
## Background

`docs/idd-workflow.md` carries two critique lenses — Mutation /
write-side, and Gate-mirroring (`#2334`). The standard C-phase reaches
them: C1 routes per-agent implementation to
`idd-overview-appendix.instructions.md`, whose Critique pass section
points at both.

Four supported configurations never see them. Three review rounds on
pull request `#2336` found them one at a time, and each was confirmed
the same way — by grepping for the **existing** lens, which is absent
too:

| Surface | State |
| --- | --- |
| lite C1 (`idd-work-lite.instructions.md`) | self-contained; never reads the appendix |
| lite E2 (`idd-review-snapshot-lite.instructions.md`) | asks for a generic critique only |
| lite E10 (`idd-review-fix-lite.instructions.md`) | self-contained critique after an E9 fix |
| a configured `critiqueLoop.delegate` | receives the branch diff, never a checklist |

`grep -rn "lens\|write-side" .github/instructions/lite/*.instructions.md`
returns nothing, so this is not a `#2334` regression: **neither lens has
ever reached the lite profile**, and the delegate surface has never
carried checklist content since `#2199` introduced it.

The delegate case is the sharper one. Under `mode: fallback` with a
successful delegate — the default — or under `never`, the per-agent
pass does not run at all, so its entire checklist is suppressed, not
just the lenses. The configured reviewer gets a diff and nothing else.

## Why a pointer will not do

`docs/weak-model-lite-profile-design.md` content principle 1 requires a
lite file to restate the load-bearing rules it depends on **inline**,
and names the standard files' "see X" pattern as the
mishandled-cross-file-reference failure mode lite exists to avoid. So
the three lite surfaces cannot be fixed by adding a link; the checks
have to be written out where they are used.

That is a real cost against the lite budgets, which is why this is its
own issue rather than a rider on `#2334`. Measured at authoring time:
`bundle-work-lite` 71.1%, `bundle-review-snapshot-lite` 94.5%,
`bundle-review-fix-lite` 95.5%, against a ceiling `audit-docs` enforces.
Two of the three have little room, so the inlined form must be the
condensed check names rather than the full prose.

## Proposed change

Restate both lenses in each of the three lite critique steps, in the
condensed form the lite profile uses elsewhere: the trigger condition
and the named checks, without the rationale paragraphs the workflow
guide carries.

For the delegate, give the configured reviewer the checklist rather than
leaving it to chance. The mechanism is a decision this issue records
rather than assumes — passing checklist content to an external command
is a new capability on that surface, and the reviewer may not accept
input at all.

## Candidate files

- `idd-template/.github/instructions/lite/idd-work-lite.instructions.md`
- `idd-template/.github/instructions/lite/idd-review-snapshot-lite.instructions.md`
- `idd-template/.github/instructions/lite/idd-review-fix-lite.instructions.md`
- `idd-template/docs/idd-workflow.md`
- `audit/sync-manifest.json`

## Acceptance criteria

- Each of lite C1, lite E2, and lite E10 states both lenses inline: the
  condition that triggers each, and its named checks. No lite file gains
  a cross-file reference for them, per content principle 1.
- The inlined check names match the workflow guide's exactly, so a
  reader applying the lite form and a reader applying the standard form
  run the same checks.
- `node scripts/sync-docs.mjs --apply` regenerates the live copies, and
  `node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check` reports no drift and every lite
  bundle within its ceiling. Any bundle that would exceed it is offset
  inside that same bundle rather than by trimming an unrelated file.
- The workflow guide records that a configured delegate does not receive
  the per-agent checklist, and what an operator should therefore expect
  from a delegate-only configuration.
- The repository `pre-push-validate` command exits clean.

## Deliberately not in scope

Changing how `critiqueLoop.delegate` invokes its command so the
checklist reaches the external reviewer. That is a capability change on
the delegate surface with its own design questions — whether the
contract passes content at all, and what happens when the reviewer
ignores it — and it should not ride along with a documentation-parity
fix. This issue documents the limitation; closing it is separate work.

Refs `#2334`, pull request `#2336`.

---

below the configured floor is human-oriented._
